title: Function-call parameter schema conventions and validation errors
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Define a single, backward-compatible canonical JSON Schema convention for function/tool call parameter definitions exposed by the Redwood API, including: 1) allowed schema keywords and our shallow extension rules (e.g., x-redwood-*), 2) deterministic validation order and error semantics, 3) runtime-friendly formats for streaming validation, and 4) a compatibility/version-negotiation strategy so older SDKs/clients can gracefully degrade when encountering new parameter features. The goal is to reduce ambiguity between model-provided 'function' specs and SDK/runtime validation layers, minimize runtime validation surprises for customers, and provide machine-readable, stable error messages for programmatic handling.
acceptance_criteria: Publish canonical JSON Schema profile (subset of Draft 2020-12) with explicit list of supported keywords and extensions
Implement validation library bindings in node/python SDKs that return standardized error objects (code, path, message, suggestion)
Define HTTP and client-visible error mapping for schema validation failures (4xx contract errors) with examples
Compatibility doc describing version negotiation header, deprecation markers in schemas, and migration steps for customers
Integration tests covering common mismatch cases (missing required, type coercion, enum mismatch, extra properties, deep nested failures)
comments: 2025-01-12 - Aisha Kumar: Initial ticket. Drafted scope after sync with product. Key constraints: keep schema subset small to avoid SDK churn; allow x-redwood-* extensions for runtime hints (e.g., x-redwood-prefetch=true). Attached initial profile doc.

2025-01-18 - Liam Chen: Added validation semantics section. Proposal: validate in deterministic order: (1) syntactic shape, (2) required fields, (3) types/coercion, (4) enum/format, (5) business constraints (pattern/min/max). On first failure return an error with path and code 'schema.invalid'. Open question: should we aggregate all failures vs fail-fast? Preferring fail-fast for streaming performance but return option to request full-report via header X-Validation-Mode=full.

2025-01-22 - PM review (Maya Ortiz): Approved approach for fail-fast default, full-report opt-in. Ask: include user-facing suggestion strings for common fixes to help integrators. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-01-28 - Design (Ravi Patel): Reviewed error UX. Suggest canonical error shape: {code, message, parameter_path, expected, received, suggestion, docs_url}. Keep suggestion short (<=140 chars) and docs_url for longer guidance. Also proposed examples for client error display.

2025-01-30 - Eng (Liam Chen): Implemented prototype validator in node SDK (schema-profile branch). Validator exposes validate(params, schema, options) -> {valid: boolean, error: string|null, details: []|null}. Pushed initial integration tests covering required/type/enum cases to PR #7421.

2025-02-02 - Security (Nina Park): Reviewed and flagged that schema extensions (x-redwood-*) must not allow executable code or remote references. Add policy: only primitive/runtime hints allowed; disallow 'x-redwood-uri' or similar. Security sign-off pending these constraints.

2025-02-03 - Liam Chen: Updated draft to explicitly forbid remote $ref resolution at runtime for production validators; allow offline precompilation in CI. Marking ticket In Review and requesting API/SDK reviewers for cross-language parity.
implementation_details: We will adopt a constrained profile of JSON Schema Draft 2020-12. Supported keywords: type, properties, required, additionalProperties (explicit true/false), enum, const, minimum/maximum, minLength/maxLength, pattern, items (single-schema), oneOf/anyOf (limited), format (email, uri, date-time), default (for clients that want autofill). Extensions: x-redwood-display_label, x-redwood-prefetch (boolean), x-redwood-deprecated (version string). Disallowed: dynamic remote $ref resolution, executable formats. Validators must support optional coercion flags (coerce_numbers=true) and a header-driven validation-mode: fail-fast (default) or full-report. Error codes: schema.invalid, schema.missing_required, schema.type_mismatch, schema.enum_mismatch, schema.extra_property, schema.pattern_mismatch, schema.range_error, schema.deprecated_field. Each error must include parameter path (JSON Pointer), expected description, actual value summary, and docs_url for remediation.
migration_notes: Compatibility strategy: (1) versioned schema in 'function.schema_version' and API header X-Redwood-Schema-Version to negotiate; (2) when new keywords are added, server must expose 'capabilities' in function metadata listing supported x-redwood-* hints; (3) clients that do not recognize a new keyword must ignore it and fallback to documented graceful-degradation behavior. Plan a 3-stage rollout: alpha (internal), beta (opt-in customers), general availability with 90 days deprecation window for removed fields.
test_plan: Unit tests for validator libs (node/python) covering 200+ variant cases; contract tests between runtime and SDK: schema roundtrip, validator parity; property-based fuzz tests for malformed schemas; end-to-end tests exercising HTTP error mapping and SDK error shaping; add telemetry to measure frequency of schema validation failures in prod for 30 days post-GA.
open_questions: Should we allow limited oneOf for union-typed params or ban for simplicity? Proposal: allow oneOf but limit to <=3 branches and require discriminator via x-redwood-discriminator when present.
Aggregation vs fail-fast: default fail-fast but full-report mode semantics need explicit timeout/size limits to avoid streaming tail latency impact.
What is the canonical HTTP status for user-provided malformed parameter payloads? Proposal: 400 with body.code = 'schema.invalid' and RFC7807-like structure.
